basics.name: Giovanni Filomeno, Ph.D.
basics.label: AI/ML Lead Engineer & Researcher
basics.summary: Specialized engineer, focused on numerical computation, optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI). Significant experience in the application of numerical methods and optimization. Growing AI expertise through industrial role and academic pursuits, including a JKU master's program and a Stanford University professional course, with a goal of leveraging acquired skills to develop innovative solutions in complex industrial contexts.

work.name: BMW Group
work.summary: Leading AI initiatives across predictive maintenance, multilingual NLP, and industrial deployment for global BMW programs.
highlights: Member of task force for Continental braking system recall; built AI models across time-series, audio, and image data achieving 91% accuracy in detecting faulty brakes (diagnostic efficiency improvement).
Extended multilingual damage classification models from 512 to 4096 tokens and implemented sliding-window processing for >10k-token documents to enhance long-context understanding.
Operationalized previously fine-tuned GPT-2 for international rollout and enabled cross-team independent deployment and usage.
Managed 500k € annual budget for strategic AI initiatives, training, and cloud services.

work.name: BMW Group
work.summary: Developed production-grade AI systems for automotive analytics, predictive maintenance, and multilingual NLP automation.
highlights: Designed and implemented AWS ETL pipeline (S3, Glue, QuickSight, Athena) processing 350+ parameters from 200,000 vehicles to optimize BMW powertrain, with projected deployment to 3 million vehicles.
Built PyTorch predictive maintenance models reducing vehicle recalls by 30% and contributed to ZF 8HP recall task force.
Implemented NLP models to classify damage reports in 10 languages (86% accuracy) and fine-tuned GPT-2 on repair protocols improving response time by 90%.
Managed 150k € annual budget for cloud computing and training; supervised 6 Master's and 1 Ph.D. students; oversaw data compliance and exchange contracts with MAGNA/ZF.

work.name: BMW Group
work.position: Research Scientist in Optimization, Modelling and Numerical Methods
work.summary: Researched optimization algorithms and design automation for electric powertrains and automotive components.
highlights: Developed mathematical model correlating component dimensions with characteristics, enabling broader solution exploration and EMI filter volume optimization.
Created bi-objective real-coded genetic algorithm for constrained component positioning, achieving 13.6% volume reduction in BMW i3 powertrain.
Validated automatic design optimization results with numerical simulations across constrained design spaces.

work.name: Siemens AG
work.position: Student Job - Advanced Modeling and Simulation
work.summary: Validated anti-smoke systems using CFD analysis to ensure compliance with customer requirements.
highlights: Performed fluid-dynamic analyses in Ansys and Star-CCM+ to validate three Siemens anti-smoke systems.

work.name: Institute of Computer Graphics - Johannes Kepler University
work.summary: Developing focus-based image segmentation methods using deep learning for stacked image datasets.
highlights: Built convolutional architectures to segment in-focus and out-of-focus regions using learned noise statistics.

work.name: Chair of Ophthalmology and Optometry - Medical University of Vienna
work.summary: Deep learning and implicit neural networks for computer-aided diagnosis and preventive retina treatment.
highlights: Implemented deep learning and implicit neural network models to identify veins and capillaries from low-resolution retina images.

work.name: Chair of Computational Modelling and Simulation - Technical University Munich
work.summary: Finite Element Method software development for advanced simulation workflows.
highlights: Implemented plasticity deformation and thermal gradient matrix routines for FEM simulation.
Implemented H-refinement and P-refinement routines and performed convergence testing.

highlights: Generative Models: VAE/GMVAE/IWAE/SSVAE, GAN, WGAN-GP, MAF; explored stability, divergences, and Wasserstein gradient penalty.
